summary: The copy claim checks out against the judge's own setup record and the s4 result, and encoding the TMA maps on the host per call is legal and graph-safe. Proceed as the land candidate, but dispatch it after the forced twin is harvested, not alongside it. Its only extra information over the forced twin is the selector's decision, and with 5 checks left that decision is worth a check only once the forced run shows wgmma rows in the judged profile.
justification: COPIES CLAIM, verified from evidence because TASK.md, AGENTS.md and rules/ never mention copies (TASK.md only says the judge runs 'steps of its own'). The source is the judge's setup record in okc.json, e.g. s4 archive/.../4e7f8be895a145ba.okc.json.gz: {event: setup, copies: 2, baseline_copies: 4, prepare_pad, prepare_s: 39.34}. Three facts follow. (1) prepare_s 39.3 s matches the log's single-prepare total ('prepare so far 39.3s'), so the second copy is most likely made by copying the prepared state, not by a second prepare(). (2) The copy count differs per side (SGLang 4, submission 2) and sits beside prepare_pad, so it looks sized from the state's memory footprint, i.e. tensors are duplicated. (3) s4 logged PATH CHOSEN = WGMMA and passed its own two-prepare replay check, yet the judged run matched master to 1e-6 (1.343894 vs 1.343895), and the profile shows only Marlin at bs=128/256 (306.2 / 483.2 us, 2 calls). That fits the stored-pointer guard _wg_state_live failing on cloned tensors. It also fits a guard that is wrong even on the original, but s5 deletes the guard, so the fix covers both. Caveat: s4's state held wg_ext (a module object), and plain copy.deepcopy cannot pickle modules. So the judge's copier is not plain deepcopy. It is more likely a container tree-map that clones tensors and passes other objects through. The self-check's state C, not state B, is the judge-like one. PER-CALL ENCODE: legal and graph-safe. cuTensorMapEncodeTiled is a pure host encoder with no stream work, no sync and no allocation. Under torch.cuda.graph it runs once at capture, and the CUtensorMap passed by value as a __grid_constant__ parameter is frozen into the kernel node. Replays never re-run host code, so the encode costs nothing in timed replays and binds each graph to the scratch of the state it was captured on. The maps derive from state scratch, not from data, so nothing derived from inputs is cached. It is ordinary launch marshalling inside kernel_fn, like Marlin's own host argument setup. MECHANISM/SHAPES: wgmma has never had a judged row; s3 died on recheck and s4 never launched. The prepare forecasts (0.63x/0.55x) come from an all-local regime where Marlin takes 921/1278 us, against judged Marlin pairs of 306/483 us, so the expected wins are unproven. The incumbent pairs are about 3x and 4.4x the floors (101.3/108.9 us), so there is room. Bucket mapping matches TASK.md: verify_16 = bs128 and verify_32 = bs256 are the only timed shapes in 128..512, and the bs=257 and skewed-128 tests exercise the gate untimed. WEAKEST LINK: the selector decides from a calibrated synthetic routing in prepare. Prepare has already mis-forecast the judge (prepare undercounts 20-25%, and the earlier wrong-regime forecasts), while the 1.02x margin is much smaller than the +-20% Marlin profile noise. If the true per-bucket gain is under about 1.2x, the gate can come out either way. A disabled bucket then gives a master-identical row and no wgmma data, which is why the forced twin must carry the measurement.
confounders: w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (9080a71, the base): changes only the T<=32 w2 call; disjoint from 128<=T<=512, so bs=1/8/16/32 are clean controls.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: tunes Marlin's block_size_m at T>=128, i.e. the incumbent the selector races. Racing the tuned incumbent is correct, not a confounder, but the selector must call master's own _moe_marlin path with master's block_size_m (16 at T=128, 32 at T=256), not a re-derived config.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / align-parallel-per-expert-verify: the wgmma path runs its own align at block 16, while master runs the parallel per-expert align at T>128. The spec calls align/combine 'shared', but it is not, so each side of the selector must be timed as its full kernel_fn graph (align included), or the A/B misattributes about 5-10 us per side. Same for reading the judged profile: sum align+gather+2x wg+norm vs align+2x Marlin+act_and_mul+norm.
interference: No companions. The forced twin is this run's control: identical code, selector off, so it gives the judged wgmma rows whatever the gate decides. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not change whether the copy fix makes wgmma launch, and none of them shares the 128..512 launch sequence except the incumbent being replaced. The real issue is sequencing under a budget of 5 checks with 5 queued. If both twins run in parallel and the forced run shows no wgmma rows (copy fix ineffective), both checks are spent on one fact. If the forced run shows wgmma slower in both buckets, this run should reproduce master and teaches nothing beyond the selector's agreement. Recommend dispatching this run only after the forced run's profile shows wgmma kernel names at bs=128/256, and only if at least one bucket is at or below the Marlin pair. If the forced run wins clearly in both buckets, this run is still the safer ship candidate, so run it then.
rules_flags: Per-call cuTensorMapEncodeTiled in kernel_fn is legal: host-only, no sync, no allocation, no stream work, derived from state scratch rather than data, and frozen into the graph at capture. Resolve the driver entry point (cudaGetDriverEntryPoint / cuGetProcAddress) once and cache the function pointer in a host static, or resolve it in prepare. Don't resolve it inside capture, so global-mode capture never meets an API it treats as unsafe. A cached PFN is not state-specific, which is allowed under the two-state rule.

Encode EVERY map the kernels read at launch time from tensors passed in that call: s4's Maps holds 4 CUtensorMaps per launch, while the spec says 'the two descriptors it needs'. If any map over a weight bank (wg_banks) or other state tensor is still pre-encoded in prepare and carried in state, a cloned copy reads the original's bank. That is harmless only while the weights stay unchanged, and it is still a latent cross-copy alias.

Removing _wg_state_live turns a copy-semantics mistake into a judge correctness failure instead of a silent Marlin fallback. That is acceptable for a check, but the three-state self-check must use a recursive dict/list/tuple tensor-clone copier that passes non-tensors by reference (state C). That copier is the one consistent with the judge copying a state that holds a module object. copy.deepcopy will likely raise on wg_ext, which is fine as long as it is caught in prepare.

Release every prepare-time graph, the >=256 MB flush buffer, the self-check states B/C and the selector scratch before prepare returns. The judge's setup record ties copy count to prepare_pad (s3 31.7 MB vs s4 2.2 MB), so leaked memory could change the copy count or exhaust memory once the state is duplicated.

The prefill precedent for per-call encode (experts-turn4 ssdq) never ran in the judge: its load_inline failed with an undefined symbol for at::TensorBase::data_ptr<long long>. Use untyped data_ptr() or data_ptr<int64_t> through the supported API, and avoid templated data_ptr<long long> in the new C++.
Selector booleans state['wg_on_128'/'wg_on_256'] are prepare-time and shape-keyed: legal. kernel_fn has no try/except, prints or syncs per spec; confirm lint shows none in kernel_fn's call graph.
open_questions: Does the judge copy by tensor tree-map (clone tensors, share everything else) or by some other route? The s4 module-in-state plus pass suggests a tree-map. Print in prepare the id() of state['wg_ext'] and the data_ptr of wg_xs, and in the judge log nothing more (no prints in kernel_fn), so a future failure can be triaged from the self-check lines alone.

Does the B128 gate's T=128 calibration represent the judged verify_16 routing well enough? Print the Marlin pair at the calibrated routing beside the judged 306.2 us (bs128) and 483.2 us (bs256) so the forecast error is readable at harvest.

If the forced twin shows wgmma rows at or below Marlin in only one bucket, does this gate enable exactly that bucket? That agreement is the only new fact this run can add, so print the per-bucket decision late in the log tail.
Prepare budget: s4 was 39 s. Three-state captures, a profiler pass and 2 buckets x 2 routings x 41 cold-flushed graph A/B reps should add well under 60 s, but print per-phase timings.
